facts.label: New equipment request in three steps
facts.description: New equipment request in three steps: equipment (with dates), project, review and submit (FDD 7.5; replaces project-create-request, request-catalog and request-cart for project requests). Posts what the old cart's INTERNAL submit posts, through the same requestHeaderBody / requestLineBody builders. ?draftId= reopens a saved project draft.

chains.name: cartChain
chains.about: The cart. One line per equipment, as the old cart keys it; items are built by catalogCart.itemFromRow, the old catalog's own builder, so a line carries the same rate, unit and period fields into requestLineBody. add from a card (quantity 1, or one more when already in the cart) inc / dec the stepper; down to 0 removes the line set a typed quantity on Review (at least 1) remove the line line a line's own start date, end date or notes; empty falls back to the request's

chains.name: enforcePageAccessChain
chains.about: Page-level RBAC deep-link guard. GENERATED - every copy is byte-identical; change the template and regenerate rather than editing one copy. Copies exist because a page's eventListeners resolve a bare chain id against that page's OWN <page>-chains folder, so an app-level chain referenced by name 404s. This file holds NO policy: the decision (canEnterPage), the page code (getPageCodeForPage), the redirect target (getRoleHomeTarget) and the same-flow test (isSameFlow) all live in $application.functions. Deriving the page code at runtime is what lets every copy be identical.

chains.name: filterCatalogChain
chains.about: Catalog search, class chip, "free on these dates only" and "Show more". Filtering itself is new-request-page.js filterCatalog; this only holds the choices.

chains.name: goStepChain
chains.about: Moves between the three steps. Back is always allowed; forward checks every step on the way (new-request-page.js missingFor) and lists what is missing instead of moving. Arriving at Review resolves the delivery point (deliveryCoords, as NavigateToCatalogChain does before the old catalog) and reloads the catalog with the project and that point, so every line shows the price this project and the nearest yard give before anything is submitted.

chains.name: loadCatalogChain
chains.about: The catalog for the chosen dates: the old catalog's endpoint and parameters (views/equipment-catalog with startDate, endDate and requestedQty=1 for availability; projectRefId for the project's rate schedule; the delivery point for nearest-yard rates). Each parameter is sent only when known, as the old CatalogInitChain does, because an undefined value goes out as the text "undefined". Then every cart line is priced again from the new rows with catalogCart.itemFromRow, keeping its quantity and its own dates and notes, so the cart never shows a price the dates or project no longer give.

chains.name: loadProjectListsChain
chains.about: The lists that hang off the chosen project, fetched together as the old CaptureProjectNameChain does: tasks Fusion projects/{id}/child/Tasks, chargeable leaves only (projectTaskTree; a summary task cannot take cost) contracts BIP EQP_CONTRACTS_BY_PROJECT_LOV_RP business unit projects/{id} (projectBusinessUnit), posted as PROJECT_BU_ID / PROJECT_BU_NAME A reopened draft that already has a contract also gets that contract's sites.

chains.name: loadSitesChain
chains.about: Ship-to sites of the chosen contract on this project (BIP EQP_SHIP_TO_SITES_BY_CONTRACT_LOV_RP, as the old LoadShipToSitesChain). The site's address is its id, so picking one sets the delivery location directly; CUSTOMER_NAME (label2) says whose site it is.

chains.name: newRequestInitChain
chains.about: Opens New request. The requestor is the signed-in user, as the old SeedRequestorChain sets it (requestorName and requestorUsername; no EQR_USER id for INTERNAL). The rate, hours and customer switches use the same app functions as the old create page and cart, once the settings and roles have loaded. With ?draftId= it reopens a saved DRAFT instead: draftResume loads the header and lines and prices them from today's catalog, and requestHeaderBody.toFlowState turns the header back into the form. Submit and Save draft then update that request in place (resume), so it keeps its number, as the old…

chains.name: pickChain
chains.about: A search result was picked (index into projectResults / customerResults), or cleared (index -1). project writes id, number and name and clears the task, contract and contract site, then loads the project's tasks, contracts and business unit (CaptureProjectNameChain) customer the Fusion CustomerId and name of the project's customer (CaptureFallbackCustomerChain)

chains.name: searchChain
chains.about: Search as you type for Project and Customer, with the old pickers' BIP reports (ProjectTypeaheadChain, CustomerTypeaheadChain): case-insensitive over name and number, P_SEARCH_BY=ALL. A short pause lets typing settle, and an answer for text the user has already changed is dropped.

chains.name: setFieldChain
chains.about: One field of the form changed (inputs carry data-field). The side effects are the old create page's: dates reload the catalog, so availability, estimates and cart prices follow the new window task keeps number and name with the id (TaskSelectedChain) contract clears a contract site and loads that contract's ship-to sites (CaptureContractChain) site the picked site's address is the delivery location (CaptureShipToSiteChain) locationType switching between a contract site and a typed address clears the address

chains.name: submitChain
chains.about: Submit for approval, or Save draft. The old cart's INTERNAL path, step for step (SubmitRequestChain and SecondaryActionChain), with the same shared builders: 1 header requestHeaderBody.saveHeader: POST createEquipmentRequest as DRAFT (PATCH for a reopened draft) 2 site geocode the address, then createShipToSite and PATCH shipToSiteId (best effort) 3 lines requestLineBody.saveLines: one batch, each line SUBMITTED (or DRAFT); a failed batch deletes a new header, so nothing half-saved is left 4 status PATCH the header to SUBMITTED (submit only). SUBMITTED, not IN_PROCESS: a project request…

modules.name: requestLineBody
modules.about: ONE builder for the createRequestLine body, shared by the cart's Submit (SubmitRequestChain) and Save as Draft (SecondaryActionChain), so a draft line stores exactly what a submitted line stores. Only lineStatus differs: Save as Draft → DRAFT (INTERNAL and EXTERNAL) Submit, INTERNAL project → SUBMITTED (an approver still has to confirm) Submit, EXTERNAL customer→ IN_PROCESS (no customer-side approver) lineStatus is set ON CREATE. modules.about: Who is the signed-in user? modules.name: draftResume
modules.about: Reopen a saved DRAFT request into the create-request flow (Edit Draft / Submit Draft on the request detail pages), and delete one (Delete Draft). The hand-off reuses the cart's own refresh-resume: InitCartChain already restores request / ActiveRequestDetail / requestOrigin / CartItemsArray from draftStorage, so writing those keys and navigating is all the cart needs. The create-request form picks the same keys up in HydrateDraftChain (case d) / CreateRequestInitChain when the tab-scoped…

modules.name: draftStorage
modules.about: Returns true if localStorage has a non-empty draft for this key. On resume pages (catalog, cart) we always prefer the persisted draft over whatever VBCS initialized the flow variable to — otherwise default values on the variable (e.g. request.creditLimit) make the variable look "non-empty" and would silently block hydration, dropping user-typed fields like `location` after a refresh.

modules.name: requestHeaderBody
modules.about: ONE builder for the createEquipmentRequest body, shared by the cart's Submit (SubmitRequestChain) and Save as Draft (SecondaryActionChain), so a draft stores everything a submitted request stores: customer, project contract, delivery mode/ids, default hours, dates, agreement. Before this, Save as Draft had its own hand-written body that dropped 11 of those fields — every draft on paasdev had no customer (2026-10-11). Both buttons create the header as DRAFT.
